title: I'm 1% of a mentor
header_line: My analysis of one book on an entrepreneur's life. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: Whose advice would you take only 1% of?

A student said the author said that when he was home he tried to put time with his kids to good use. I said: he's going to paint it like that a little bit. But I think there were sacrifices. We can't judge, I said. We don't know.
I asked: think about the time you spend with your kids without your phone, without distractions. You can justify it, I said. But are you really having in-depth conversations?

Learning about different people in their lives, I said, you go: I want this, but I don't want that. I want ten percent from this mentor and I'll leave out the other ninety. I tell my kids: I am one percent of a mentor. Go and get the ninety-nine. But that one percent is a big deal.
A student said a telltale sign of how you see your family is what you do without them.

I said a common denominator among my friends and business partners is an effort to be good fathers. A friend of mine told his kids: we're going on a trip, you are welcome to come if you like. He said he learned a lesson from it, because he used to make it mandatory.
Are we around people in this culture where we are all go-getters, I asked, obsessed with the job, developing good habits, going a hundred and fifty miles an hour as an organization, or going twenty?
The reports tell us who is showing up and who is not, I said. Those checks and balances are necessary, and they make sure you keep your promises to yourself.
You can't say: I'd like to make a couple of million dollars in twenty-four months, but you're not making the calls. Then you're not in the possibility game. So as a team we need accountability.
What is the one percent you will take from each mentor?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write two mentors or people you learn from.
Write the ten percent you will take from each, and the ninety you will leave.
Write how much undistracted time you give the people who matter most.
Write one promise to yourself, and who will check it.
Write one number you can report on weekly.

check.q: What did I say I am to my kids?
What did I say the reports and checks and balances help you do?
What did I say about time with your kids?
choices: Think about the time without your phone or distractions

recap: Take the one percent that matters from each mentor, and keep your promises to yourself.
